Axiom: The SDD mechanical tools are `gennady` CLI commands. When working IN the gennady repo itself (including any worktree), the runner is `npx tsx /cli/gennady.ts`; in every other project it is `npx gennady`. Thus a Step's canonical `npx gennady ` fixes the command and arguments exactly; substitute only this runner when developing gennady itself, using the current worktree's root. Tools: `sdd-state`, `sdd-task`, `sdd-extract`, `sdd-verify`, `sdd-log`, `sdd-sync`, `sdd-check`, `sdd-new`, `sdd-migrate`, `sdd-orient`, `sdd-session`, `orient`, `lint`, `yagni`, `testcov`. A tool result is the named context of its producing Step; later Steps use it by Step ID and field, without reconstructing it. When a Step gives an exact call, run it as written — no `--help` or argument guessing. Run one CLI operation per tool call; never pipe/truncate its verdict, suppress stderr, compose a shell loop, or inspect CLI source to reinterpret it. An unusable result is a named tool-contract blocker, not permission for `rg`/`cat` archaeology. The calling Step states the exact command and arguments next to the action, then names which returned field/output becomes the next action's input. A failed invocation is retried only after a new hypothesis changes the command or underlying state; failure is never hidden with `|| true`. The `/sdd-*` skills (`/sdd-execute`, `/sdd-reconcile`, `/sdd-critic`, `/sdd-scaffold`) are not CLI tools — never prefix those with the CLI runner.
